synth.title: Synth
synth.intro: The instrument: scope, three strings, chord pads and the loop pedal. This is the page the app opens on.

hdr_sound.title: SOUND NAME
hdr_sound.summary: The current sound, its slot and how the keys play.
hdr_sound.does: Name, slot (Sound 1-10, or Unsaved) and the key mode: Strings (one note per row, slides) or Poly (every key its own note). Tags: REC, Limit, No audio device.

use.text: Tap the header to open the Sound page.
Press 1-9 or 0 to jump to sound 1-10.
Ctrl+P switches Strings and Poly.

hdr_sound.recall: Synth page, top left. Ctrl+Z undoes a sound change. Limit: lower Master volume.
tips: A name ending in * is a mutated copy of another sound.
hdr_sound.ask: What do the Limit and No audio device tags mean?

hdr_tune.title: KEY / SCALE / TEMPO
hdr_tune.summary: Root note, scale, tempo with a lamp, and octave.
hdr_tune.does: Left to right: the key's root note, the scale name (min pent = minor pentatonic), tempo in beats per minute with a lamp that flashes on each beat while something plays, and the octave shift.

use.text: Tap the header to open the Tune page, where all of it can be changed.
Ctrl+K key up, Ctrl+S next scale, Ctrl+T tap tempo, Up/Down octave.

hdr_tune.recall: Synth page, top right. Full controls: Tune tab. Key and scale also change with Ctrl+K and Ctrl+S.
tips: Add Shift to Ctrl+K or Ctrl+S to step the other way.
hdr_tune.ask: How do the key and scale change what I can play?

xy.title: SCOPE / TOUCH PAD
xy.summary: Drag to change the sound while you play: two controls at once.
xy.does: The scope draws the real output. Drag on it: left-right and bottom-top each move a control, set by the mapping button (Filter: cutoff, resonance). Let go and it returns, unless Hold is on.

use.text: Drag anywhere on the scope.
Ctrl+G cycles the mapping.

xy.recall: Synth page, the big box. Mapping: corner button or System page.
tips: Moves are recorded into a loop.
xy.ask: What does dragging on the scope actually change?

xymap.title: MAPPING BUTTON
xymap.summary: Picks which two controls the scope pad moves.
xymap.does: Cycles Filter, Wobble, Morph, Space, Bend, Glitch. Each sets what left-right (X) and bottom-top (Y) do; the faint Y and X labels on the scope name them. The name on the button is the active one.

use.text: Tap to step to the next mapping; it wraps around.
Ctrl+G does the same from any page.

xymap.recall: Scope corner on the Synth page; also System page, Touch pad mapping (pick one directly). Ctrl+G steps on.
tips: System page lists all six with their X/Y pair in one row.
xymap.ask: What does each touch pad mapping do?

xyhold.title: HOLD
xyhold.summary: Keeps the pad's last position after you lift your finger.
xyhold.does: Off: the sound goes back to normal when you let go. On: the last X-Y position stays applied (a filter held half shut, glitch left on) until you turn Hold off or move the pad again.

use.text: Tap to switch on or off; lit means on.

xyhold.recall: Synth page scope corner, and System page next to the mappings. Tap again to release.
tips: With Glitch mapped, Hold leaves the crush on until you release it.
xyhold.ask: When should I use Hold on the touch pad?

scopeview.title: SCOPE VIEW
scopeview.summary: Cycles the scope: 3D, spectrum, waterfall, phase, level, line.
scopeview.does: Every view draws your real output. 3D: recent cycles stacked. SPEC: frequencies, with the filter cutoff. FALL: spectra stacked. PHASE: a loop figure. LEVEL: loudness, 4 s. LINE: the moving line.

use.text: Tap for the next view; the key shows its name.
Ctrl+V next view. Hold Ctrl+C to open the filter, Ctrl+X to close it.

scopeview.recall: Synth page, top right of the scope, left of the mapping key.
tips: Hold a note with Space, then hold Ctrl+C: in SPEC the peaks follow the cutoff.
scopeview.ask: What do the scope views show?

string2.title: HIGH STRING (S3)
string2.summary: Top string: Q to P. Ten notes, left to right goes up the scale.
string2.does: One monophonic string: it sounds one note at a time. Press a note box to play, or a key. Hold one and press another on the string and the note slides without restarting; release the newer key and it slides back.

use.text: Press to play; drag to slide.
Q to P. Shift for semitones.

string2.recall: Synth page, top string. On the Q20 these are the top letter row. Backspace stops stuck notes.
tips: Bright frames mark the root; brackets show the real pitch.
string2.ask: How do slides work on the strings?

string1.title: MIDDLE STRING (S2)
string1.summary: Middle string: A to L. Nine notes in the scale.
string1.does: The middle of three strings. Strings are tuned a set gap apart (5 semitones by default, Tune page). Same rules as the others: one note at a time, a second key on the row slides it.

use.text: Press to play; drag to slide.
A to L. Hold one, tap another to slide.

string1.recall: Synth page, middle string. Change spacing in Tune, String gap.
tips: Hold a note on each row to glide a chord.
string1.ask: How are the three strings tuned against each other?

string0.title: LOW STRING (S1)
string0.summary: Bottom string: Z to M. Seven notes, the lowest range.
string0.does: The lowest string. It starts one key in on screen to line up with the Q20 keyboard. With the chord row on (the $ key) or Alt held, these keys play the chord pads instead of notes.

use.text: Press a note box; drag to slide.
Z X C V B N M. Alt + a key plays chord I-VII; $ toggles chord row.

string0.recall: Synth page, bottom string. Chord row on: label tags show on these keys; $ switches it off.
tips: On the Pulse page this row still plays notes.
string0.ask: How do I make the bottom row play chords?

chord0.title: CHORD PADS I-VII
chord0.summary: The seven chords of your key; what a tap does depends on mode.
chord0.does: Each pad shows a chord and its numeral (small = minor). Prog: a tap adds it to a looping progression of up to eight. Hold: latches one chord. Drone: toggles its root as a held note.

use.text: Tap a pad. Mode: the button beside the pads.
Alt+Z..M: chords I to VII.

chord0.recall: Synth and Backing pages. Clear all on the Backing page clears; Ctrl+Backspace removes the last chord.
tips: Chords follow the key and scale.
chord0.ask: What do the chord pads do in each mode?

loop_pedal.title: LOOP PEDAL
loop_pedal.summary: One button to record, play and layer a loop.
loop_pedal.does: Tap: count-in, then it records your playing (notes, slides, bends, pad moves). Tap again to close the loop at the end of the bar. Next taps overdub a layer, then finish it. The label shows what the next tap does.

use.text: Tap Loop; the label shows the next step.
Enter = tap. Ctrl+L stop/start, Ctrl+D clear.

loop_pedal.recall: Synth page, bottom left. Undo removes the last layer; Ctrl+D erases the loop. Volume: System page.
tips: Up to 64 bars and six layers, each with its own sound.
loop_pedal.ask: How do I record and layer a loop?

loop_undo.title: LOOP UNDO
loop_undo.does: Takes off the newest overdub layer, one tap per layer, back to the first take. Only affects the loop, not your sound.

use.text: Tap Undo to peel off one layer.
Ctrl+U.

loop_undo.recall: Synth page, bottom row, second button. Ctrl+U. Ctrl+D erases the whole loop.
loop_undo.ask: How do I undo a loop layer?

loop_playstop.title: LOOP PLAY / STOP
loop_playstop.summary: Starts or stops the loop without erasing it.
loop_playstop.does: Shows a stop square while the loop plays and a play triangle otherwise. Stopping keeps every layer; start plays it again from the top, in time with the tempo.

use.text: Tap to stop or restart.
Ctrl+L.

loop_playstop.recall: Synth page, bottom row, third button. Ctrl+L. Ctrl+D erases the loop for good.
loop_playstop.ask: How do I stop the loop and start it again?

sustain.title: SUSTAIN
sustain.summary: Keeps notes ringing after you let go.
sustain.does: While on, released notes keep sounding, and a new key on a ringing string slides that note instead of starting a new one. Tap to latch on; tap again to release. Holding Space does the same while held.

use.text: Tap to latch on or off; inverted means on.
Hold Space. Backspace (panic) turns the latch off.

sustain.recall: Synth page, bottom row. Space while held. Backspace silences everything and clears the latch.
tips: Sustain plus slides makes a good slow glissando.
sustain.ask: What does sustain do when I play slides?

octave_down.title: OCTAVE - / +
octave_down.summary: Shifts the whole instrument one octave down or up.
octave_down.does: Moves every string by 12 semitones, up to three octaves each way. Held notes sweep to the new octave without restarting. The octave number shows top right in the header.

use.text: Tap - for lower, + for higher.
Down / Up arrows, or - and =.

octave_down.recall: Synth page bottom row; also Tune page, Octave. Arrows are on the Q20's symbol layer.
tips: Octave range is -3 to +3.
octave_down.ask: How far can I shift the octave?

new_sound.title: NEW SOUND
new_sound.does: Builds a complete new playable sound, loudness-matched so it is not louder than the others. The old sound goes on the undo stack. It is Unsaved until you Store or Save it.

use.text: Tap New.
Ctrl+R. Ctrl+Z goes back; Ctrl+N nudges instead.

new_sound.recall: Synth page, bottom row; Sound page, New sound. Ctrl+Z undoes it (24 steps). Ctrl+F keeps it.
tips: Like one? Press Ctrl+F before you roll again.
new_sound.ask: How do I keep a random sound I like?

menu.title: MENU
menu.summary: Opens the Sound page and the tab strip to other pages.
menu.does: The Synth page has no tab strip, so Menu takes you to the Sound page, which shows the tabs for Synth, Sound, Pulse, Tune, System, Help and Chat.

use.text: Tap Menu, then choose a tab.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc comes back here.

menu.recall: Synth page, bottom right. Esc from any page returns to Synth.
menu.ask: How do I get to the other pages from here?

key_readout.title: KEY READOUT
key_readout.summary: The root note and scale every string is locked to.
key_readout.does: Shows the key (A, C#...) and the scale in short form, like min pent. Every string plays only notes of this scale, so nothing sounds wrong.

use.text: Tap it to open the Tune page and change key or scale.
Ctrl+K raises the key a semitone; Ctrl+S picks the next scale.

key_readout.recall: Top of the Synth page, left of the tempo. Same controls: Tune page.
tips: Shift with Ctrl+K lowers the key.
key_readout.ask: How does the scale lock work?

tempo_readout.title: TEMPO READOUT
tempo_readout.summary: The speed of the loop and the tempo sync, in bpm.
tempo_readout.does: Shows the tempo. The small square beside it blinks on the beat while anything is running. One tempo drives the loop pedal, the pulse pads' SYNC, the delay and the click.

use.text: Tap it to open the Tune page, where tempo has - and + and Tap.
Ctrl+T taps the tempo with the beat of your finger.

tempo_readout.recall: Top of the Synth page, between key and octave. Also on the Tune page.
tips: Two taps already set it; more taps average out (within 2 seconds).
tempo_readout.ask: How do I change the tempo?

octave_readout.title: OCTAVE READOUT
octave_readout.summary: How many octaves the whole instrument is shifted.
octave_readout.does: Shows 0 at rest, or +1, -2... up to three octaves each way. It moves every string together, so a part can sit higher or lower without changing keys.

use.text: Tap it to open the Tune page. The - and + buttons are at the bottom of Synth.
Down and Up arrows, or - and =.

octave_readout.recall: Top right of the Synth page. Buttons: bottom row of Synth, and the Tune page.
tips: Held notes sweep to the new octave without restarting.
octave_readout.ask: How far can I shift the octave?

pslot0.title: PROGRESSION SLOTS
pslot0.summary: The chords you queued, up to eight. Tap to select one.
pslot0.does: Each filled slot shows a chord name; the playing one is inverted. Tap a slot to select it (double frame), then tap a chord pad to replace it. Tap the selected slot again to deselect.

use.text: Tap a filled slot, then a chord pad to swap it.

pslot0.recall: Synth page, strip above the chord pads; also Backing page. Ctrl+Backspace removes the last chord.
tips: Empty slots show only their number and cannot be tapped.
pslot0.ask: How do I change one chord in my progression?

backmode.title: CHORD MODE
backmode.summary: Prog, Hold or Drone: what a chord tap does.
backmode.does: Prog adds taps to a looping progression. Hold plays one chord until you pick another (tap it again to stop). Drone switches a held bass note for each chord you tap on and off.

use.text: Tap to step Prog, Hold, Drone.
Ctrl+B steps the mode.

backmode.recall: Synth page, beside the pads; three buttons on the Backing page. Ctrl+B steps it.
tips: Mode names appear as a toast when you use Ctrl+B.
backmode.ask: What is the difference between Prog, Hold and Drone?

backplay.title: BACKING PLAY / STOP
backplay.summary: Starts and stops the backing chords.
backplay.does: Plays the progression (or held chord or drones) in time with the tempo, on the chord length set in Backing. Tapping a chord in Prog mode already starts it, so Play then stops it.

use.text: Tap to start or stop; inverted while playing.
Ctrl+Space toggles it from any page.

backplay.recall: Synth page and Backing page, beside the chord pads. Ctrl+Space.
tips: Backing joins the bar in progress if a loop or synced pulses are already running.
backplay.ask: Why does the backing start when I tap a chord?

synth.recall: The app opens here. From any other page press Esc, or tap the Synth tab.

sound.title: Sound
sound.intro: Pick a sound, make a new one and shape it. Ten slots, five quick-change sliders on one page, favourites below, and all parameters on request.

tab_synth.title: PAGE TABS
tab_synth.summary: The strip of seven tabs along the top.
tab_synth.does: Synth, Sound, Pulse, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_synth.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all seven; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_synth.ask: What is on each of the pages?

slot0.title: SOUND SLOTS 1-0
slot0.summary: Ten stored sounds. Tap one to play with it.
slot0.does: Each slot holds a complete sound, shown by name with its key number in the corner (slot 10 is key 0). Tapping loads it for all three strings. Edits are not saved to the slot unless you Store them.

use.text: Tap a slot. With Store armed, tapping a slot saves your sound there.
Press 1-9 or 0 (the Q20 number layer).

slot0.recall: Sound page, top two rows, or digit keys. Re-tap a slot to reload it. System > Factory sounds restores all ten.
tips: Loading a slot goes on the undo stack: Ctrl+Z comes back.
slot0.ask: What is stored in a sound slot?

newsound.title: NEW SOUND
newsound.summary: Invents a complete new random instrument.
newsound.does: Builds a new playable sound every tap and loudness-matches it. Good for exploring: roll until something good appears. The previous sound is kept on the undo stack. It is not stored until you Store or Save it.

use.text: Tap New sound.
Ctrl+R.

newsound.recall: Sound page, first button of the row; Synth page, New. Ctrl+R. Ctrl+Z steps back up to 24 times.
tips: Heard one you like? Save it before the next roll.
newsound.ask: How does New sound pick what it makes?

mutate.title: MUTATE
mutate.summary: Nudges the current sound a little.
mutate.does: Randomly changes some settings of the current sound by a small amount, so it stays recognisable but different. A star is added to its name. Repeat to wander further; undo to go back.

use.text: Tap Mutate.
Ctrl+N.

mutate.recall: Sound page, second button. Ctrl+N. Ctrl+Z goes back a step.
tips: Mutate then Save keeps a variation as a favourite.
mutate.ask: How much does Mutate change the sound?

undosound.title: UNDO SOUND
undosound.summary: Goes back to the previous sound.
undosound.does: Steps back through whole-sound changes: New sound, Mutate, picking a slot or recalling a favourite. The button shows how many steps are stored (up to 24). It does not undo slider moves or Store.

use.text: Tap Undo; repeat to go further back.
Ctrl+Z.

undosound.recall: Sound page, third button. Ctrl+Z from any page. There is no redo.
tips: Storing into a slot cannot be undone: System > Factory sounds restores the originals.
undosound.ask: What can Undo bring back, and what can it not?

slotsave.title: STORE TO SLOT
slotsave.summary: Arms the next slot tap to save your sound there.
slotsave.does: Tap Store (it shows pick a slot), then tap one of the ten slots: your current sound replaces that slot's sound. This replaces it for good and cannot be undone. Tapping another tab cancels it.

use.text: Tap Store, then tap a slot. Tap Store again to cancel.

slotsave.recall: Sound page, fourth button. Put the factory sounds back: System > Factory sounds.
tips: To keep without replacing a slot, use Save (a favourite).
slotsave.ask: How do I put my sound on a number key?

fav.title: SAVE FAVOURITE
fav.summary: Keeps the current sound in the favourites list.
fav.does: Saves the sound as a file in your favourites folder and adds it to the list at the bottom of the page. It does not replace any slot. Favourites survive restarts.

use.text: Tap Save.
Ctrl+F from any page.

fav.recall: Sound page, last button; list at the bottom of the page. Ctrl+F. Remove with Delete, then the favourite.
tips: Saving under a name you already have updates that favourite; it does not add a copy.
fav.ask: What is the difference between Store and Save?

deep.title: ALL PARAMETERS
deep.summary: Switches between eight quick sliders and every parameter.
deep.does: Quick controls are eight sliders. All parameters shows all 40 in pages of 12 (oscillators, envelopes, filter, modulation, effects), with Prev and Next below. Same sound either way.

use.text: Tap to switch; the button then says Quick controls.

deep.recall: Sound page, right of the sound name. Leaving the Sound tab returns to quick controls.
tips: Settings you change here are on the current sound only until you Store or Save it.
deep.ask: Where do I find every sound parameter?

param16.title: CUTOFF
param16.summary: How bright or dark the sound is.
param16.does: The filter's cutoff frequency, 40 Hz to 16 kHz. Low cutoff is dark and muffled; high is bright and open. The X axis of the Filter touch pad mapping moves it live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param16.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.2/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Drag it while holding a note to hear the sweep.
param16.ask: What does CUTOFF do to the sound?

param17.title: RESO
param17.does: Resonance boosts a narrow band around the cutoff. Low is smooth; high makes the filter whistle and ring, especially when moving the cutoff. Up to 95%.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param17.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.2/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Very high RESO plus low CUTOFF can be piercing.
param17.ask: What does RESO do to the sound?

param11.title: ATTACK
param11.summary: How fast a note fades in.
param11.does: Attack is the time from pressing a key to full volume, 1 ms to 4 s. Short is a clear click or pluck; long is a slow swell like a pad. The scale is logarithmic.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param11.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.2/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Attack above 300 ms makes quick playing disappear.
param11.ask: What does ATTACK do to the sound?

param14.title: RELEASE
param14.summary: How long a note fades after you let go.
param14.does: Release is the fade-out time, 10 ms to 8 s. Short stops the sound at once; long lets notes ring on and blur together.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param14.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.2/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Dream sounds use long releases; shorten them for tight playing.
param14.ask: What does RELEASE do to the sound?

param31.title: GLIDE
param31.does: Portamento: how long the pitch takes to travel when you slide from one note to another, 0 to 2000 ms. Short is a quick snap; long is a slow, swooping slide. Tune's Glide speed scales every sound.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param31.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: 0 gives instant jumps without a slide.
param31.ask: What does GLIDE do to the sound?

param32.title: DRIVE
param32.does: Saturation squashes the wave: 0 is clean, low is warm, high is gritty and fuzzy. The Morph touch pad mapping adds drive live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param32.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Drive adds loudness; watch the Limit tag.
param32.ask: What does DRIVE do to the sound?

param34.title: DELAY
param34.does: Delay repeats the sound after a pause, 0 to 70%. Echo spacing follows the tempo: set it with DLY TIME. The X axis of the Space touch pad mapping adds delay live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param34.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Slow, sparse playing sounds best with echoes.
param34.ask: What does DELAY do to the sound?

param37.title: REVERB
param37.does: Reverb adds the sense of a space, 0 to 80%. Low is a small room; high washes the sound out. The Y axis of the Space touch pad mapping adds reverb live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param37.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Pull this down if the sound feels washed out.
param37.ask: What does REVERB do to the sound?

favitem0.title: FAVOURITES
favitem0.summary: Your saved sounds. Tap one to recall it.
favitem0.does: Up to six show at once (three across, two rows). Tapping loads that sound as your current one and puts the old one on the undo stack. Starts with five dream sounds: Haze, Fuzz, Teeth, Bend and Grain.

use.text: Tap a favourite to play with it. After Delete, tap one to remove it.

favitem0.recall: Sound page, bottom area. To remove one: Delete, then tap it. Factory sounds restores dream sounds.
tips: Dream sounds are slow, soft, washed-out. Lower Reverb if too thick.
favitem0.ask: How do favourites differ from slots?

favprev.title: FAVOURITES PAGE
favprev.summary: Turns to the other six favourites.
favprev.does: Shows the page number and count, like 1/2. Tap the left half to go back a page and the right half to go forward; both wrap round.

use.text: Tap the right half for the next page, the left half for the previous one.

favprev.recall: Sound page, above Delete. Wraps around both ways.
favprev.ask: Why do some favourites not show?

favdel.title: DELETE FAVOURITE
favdel.summary: Arms the next favourite tap to delete it.
favdel.does: Tap Delete (it shows pick one and the favourites show tap to delete), then tap the favourite to remove its file for good. It disarms after one delete.

use.text: Tap Delete, then the favourite. Tap Delete again to cancel.

favdel.recall: Sound page, bottom right. A deleted dream sound returns with System > Factory sounds.
tips: Delete disarms by itself when you leave the page.
favdel.ask: How do I delete a favourite I do not want?

sound.recall: Sound tab, or tap the sound name or Menu on Synth. Keys 1-0 pick the ten slots.

sound-deep.title: Sound editor
sound-deep.intro: Every parameter of a sound, twelve to a page, with Prev and Next. Reached from the Sound tab: All parameters.

Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_synth.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all seven; Esc returns to Synth.

slot0.recall: Sound page, top two rows, or digit keys. Re-tap a slot to reload it. System > Factory sounds restores all ten.

use.text: Tap New sound.
Ctrl+R.

newsound.recall: Sound page, first button of the row; Synth page, New. Ctrl+R. Ctrl+Z steps back up to 24 times.

Ctrl+N.

Ctrl+Z.

undosound.ask: What can Undo bring back, and what can it not?

slotsave.title: STORE TO SLOT
slotsave.summary: Arms the next slot tap to save your sound there.
slotsave.does: Tap Store (it shows pick a slot), then tap one of the ten slots: your current sound replaces that slot's sound. This replaces it for good and cannot be undone. Tapping another tab cancels it.

use.text: Tap Store, then tap a slot. Tap Store again to cancel.

slotsave.recall: Sound page, fourth button. Put the factory sounds back: System > Factory sounds.
tips: To keep without replacing a slot, use Save (a favourite).
slotsave.ask: How do I put my sound on a number key?

fav.title: SAVE FAVOURITE
fav.summary: Keeps the current sound in the favourites list.
fav.does: Saves the sound as a file in your favourites folder and adds it to the list at the bottom of the page. It does not replace any slot. Favourites survive restarts.

use.text: Tap Save.
Ctrl+F from any page.

fav.recall: Sound page, last button; list at the bottom of the page. Ctrl+F. Remove with Delete, then the favourite.
tips: Saving under a name you already have updates that favourite; it does not add a copy.
fav.ask: What is the difference between Store and Save?

deep.title: ALL PARAMETERS
deep.summary: Switches between eight quick sliders and every parameter.
deep.does: Quick controls are eight sliders. All parameters shows all 40 in pages of 12 (oscillators, envelopes, filter, modulation, effects), with Prev and Next below. Same sound either way.

use.text: Tap to switch; the button then says Quick controls.

deep.recall: Sound page, right of the sound name. Leaving the Sound tab returns to quick controls.
tips: Settings you change here are on the current sound only until you Store or Save it.
deep.ask: Where do I find every sound parameter?

deepprev.title: PREV PAGE
deepprev.does: All parameters runs over four pages of twelve: oscillators and attack; envelopes and filter; modulation, glide, drive, chorus; then feedback, reverb and level. Prev goes back and wraps around.

use.text: Tap Prev.

deepprev.recall: Sound > All parameters, bottom left. Page number shows between the buttons.
deepprev.ask: What is on each page of All parameters?

deepnext.title: NEXT PAGE
deepnext.does: Goes on to the next of the four pages, wrapping to the first after the last. Page 1: oscillators and attack. Page 2: envelope and filter. Page 3: modulation, glide, drive, chorus, delay time. Page 4: feedback, reverb, level.

use.text: Tap Next.

deepnext.ask: Which page has the filter settings?

param0.title: WAVE A
param0.does: The oscillator is the tone source. Sine is pure and soft, triangle is mellow, saw is bright and buzzy, square is hollow and reedy. The slider steps through the four shapes.

use.text: Drag along the bar: it clicks through its steps; the name shows at the right.

param0.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Saw or square into a low cutoff is the classic synth lead.
param0.ask: What does WAVE A do to the sound?

param1.title: WAVE B
param1.does: Oscillator B has its own shape (sine, triangle, saw, square). You hear it when B MIX is above zero; it also drives the FM effect, even at zero mix.

use.text: Drag along the bar: it clicks through its steps; the name shows at the right.

param1.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Set B PITCH to +12 for an octave of shimmer.
param1.ask: What does WAVE B do to the sound?

param2.title: B MIX
param2.summary: Blend between oscillator A and B.
param2.does: 0% is only A, 100% only B, in between is both together. The Morph touch pad mapping moves this live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param2.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Small B MIX plus a little DETUNE gives a fat, slowly beating tone.
param2.ask: What does B MIX do to the sound?

param3.title: B PITCH
param3.does: Shifts B from -12 to +24 semitones against A. +12 is an octave up, +7 a fifth up, -12 an octave down. Whole steps only.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param3.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Fifths and octaves sound sweet; odd values sound dissonant.
param3.ask: What does B PITCH do to the sound?

param4.title: DETUNE
param4.summary: Nudges oscillator B slightly out of tune.
param4.does: Raises B by up to 50 cents (100 cents is one semitone). A tiny detune makes A and B beat against each other, which sounds thicker and alive. It only changes B.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param4.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Around 5 to 12 cents is the thick-but-in-tune range.
param4.ask: What does DETUNE do to the sound?

param5.title: UNISON
param5.summary: Adds a second copy of oscillator A.
param5.does: Blends in a duplicate of A tuned slightly off by SPREAD. At 0 you hear one voice; higher gives a wider, fatter, chorus-like sound.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param5.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Needs SPREAD above 0 to be audible.
param5.ask: What does UNISON do to the sound?

param6.title: SPREAD
param6.summary: How far the UNISON copy is detuned.
param6.does: Sets the detune of the unison copy, 0 to 40 cents. More spread is wider and more swirly. You hear nothing from it while UNISON is at 0.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param6.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Pair high UNISON with 10 to 20 cents.
param6.ask: What does SPREAD do to the sound?

param7.title: SUB
param7.summary: A sine one octave below the note.
param7.does: Mixes in a pure low sine an octave under what you play. Adds weight and body, especially on bass sounds. 0 is off.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param7.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Small speakers may not reproduce very low notes.
param7.ask: What does SUB do to the sound?

param8.title: NOISE
param8.does: Adds random noise, 0 to 60%. A little gives a breathy or plucked edge; a lot turns the sound into a wind or snare-like rush. Shaped by the filter.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param8.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Short decay plus noise makes percussion.
param8.ask: What does NOISE do to the sound?

param9.title: WIDTH
param9.summary: Pulse width of the square wave.
param9.does: Changes how wide the high part of a SQUARE wave is, 10 to 90%. 50% is a hollow clarinet tone; low or high is thin and nasal. It has no effect on other wave shapes.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param9.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: LFO>WID can sweep this for a shimmering tone.
param9.ask: What does WIDTH do to the sound?

param10.title: FM
param10.does: Frequency modulation: B wobbles A's pitch very fast, adding bell-like and metallic overtones. 0 is off, 6 is harsh and clangorous. B PITCH changes the character; B MIX does not matter.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param10.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Try FM 1 to 2 with B PITCH +12 for glassy bells.
param10.ask: What does FM do to the sound?

param11.title: ATTACK
param11.summary: How fast a note fades in.
param11.does: Attack is the time from pressing a key to full volume, 1 ms to 4 s. Short is a clear click or pluck; long is a slow swell like a pad. The scale is logarithmic.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param11.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.2/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Attack above 300 ms makes quick playing disappear.
param11.ask: What does ATTACK do to the sound?

param12.title: DECAY
param12.summary: How fast a note falls to its sustain level.
param12.does: After the attack peak the volume falls to SUSTAIN over this time, 10 ms to 6 s. Short decay with low sustain is a pluck; long is a gentle sag.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param12.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Decay does nothing if SUSTAIN is 100%.
param12.ask: What does DECAY do to the sound?

param13.title: SUSTAIN
param13.summary: The volume held while a key stays down.
param13.does: 0 to 100% of the peak. At 0 the note dies away on its own like a plucked string; at 100% it stays full until you let go.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param13.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Use DECAY with low SUSTAIN for a pluck.
param13.ask: What does SUSTAIN do to the sound?

param14.title: RELEASE
param14.summary: How long a note fades after you let go.
param14.does: Release is the fade-out time, 10 ms to 8 s. Short stops the sound at once; long lets notes ring on and blur together.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param14.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.2/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Dream sounds use long releases; shorten them for tight playing.
param14.ask: What does RELEASE do to the sound?

param15.title: FILTER
param15.summary: Type of filter: low, high or band.
param15.does: A filter removes part of the sound. LOW passes bass and cuts treble (darker). HIGH cuts bass (thinner). BAND keeps a slice in the middle (nasal, radio-like). The slider steps through them.

use.text: Drag along the bar: it clicks through its steps; the name shows at the right.

param15.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: LOW is the usual choice.
param15.ask: What does FILTER do to the sound?

param16.title: CUTOFF
param16.summary: How bright or dark the sound is.
param16.does: The filter's cutoff frequency, 40 Hz to 16 kHz. Low cutoff is dark and muffled; high is bright and open. The X axis of the Filter touch pad mapping moves it live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param16.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.2/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Drag it while holding a note to hear the sweep.
param16.ask: What does CUTOFF do to the sound?

param17.title: RESO
param17.does: Resonance boosts a narrow band around the cutoff. Low is smooth; high makes the filter whistle and ring, especially when moving the cutoff. Up to 95%.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param17.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.2/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Very high RESO plus low CUTOFF can be piercing.
param17.ask: What does RESO do to the sound?

param18.title: F.ENV
param18.summary: How far each note sweeps the filter.
param18.does: The filter envelope opens (positive) or closes (negative) the cutoff by up to 6 or -4 octaves on every note, following F.ATK, F.DEC and F.SUS. 0 means no sweep.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param18.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Positive F.ENV with short F.DEC gives a plucky wow.
param18.ask: What does F.ENV do to the sound?

param19.title: F.ATK
param19.does: How long the filter takes to reach its peak sweep after a note starts, 1 ms to 4 s. Longer gives a slow brightening.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param19.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Only audible when F.ENV is not 0.
param19.ask: What does F.ATK do to the sound?

param20.title: F.DEC
param20.does: How long the filter takes to fall from its peak to the F.SUS level, 10 ms to 6 s. Short is a quick pluck; long is a slow fade of brightness.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param20.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Only audible when F.ENV is not 0.
param20.ask: What does F.DEC do to the sound?

param21.title: F.SUS
param21.does: How much of the sweep stays while the key is held, 0 to 100%. At 0 the filter returns to the base CUTOFF; at 100% it stays fully open.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param21.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Only audible when F.ENV is not 0.
param21.ask: What does F.SUS do to the sound?

param22.title: F.REL
param22.does: How the filter moves after you let go, 10 ms to 8 s. Short snaps the brightness shut; long lets it close slowly with the tail.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param22.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Only audible when F.ENV is not 0.
param22.ask: What does F.REL do to the sound?

param23.title: K.TRACK
param23.does: Key tracking: 0 keeps the cutoff fixed; 100% moves it one octave for every octave you play, so high notes stay as bright as low ones. Middle C (C4) is the pivot.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param23.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Low K.TRACK makes high notes dull.
param23.ask: What does K.TRACK do to the sound?

param24.title: VIB HZ
param24.does: How fast vibrato, the pitch wobble, cycles: 0.5 to 9 times a second. Slow is a gentle waver; fast is a nervous shake. Only audible when VIBRATO is above 0.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param24.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: 5 to 6 Hz sounds like a singer.
param24.ask: What does VIB HZ do to the sound?

param25.title: VIBRATO
param25.does: How far the pitch wobbles each side, 0 to 60 cents (100 cents is one semitone). The Wobble touch pad mapping adds extra vibrato live, on top of this.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param25.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: 5 to 10 cents is subtle and expressive.
param25.ask: What does VIBRATO do to the sound?

param26.title: VIB DLY
param26.does: Seconds, 0 to 2, before the vibrato starts after a note begins; it then fades in over a quarter second. Like a singer holding a note straight, then wavering.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param26.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Zero gives vibrato from the first instant.
param26.ask: What does VIB DLY do to the sound?

param27.title: LFO HZ
param27.does: The LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is a slow wobble generator, 0.05 to 12 times a second. It drives LFO>CUT, LFO>AMP and LFO>WID, so nothing is heard unless one of them is above 0.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param27.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Match the delay: 1 Hz is one wobble a second.
param27.ask: What does LFO HZ do to the sound?

param28.title: LFO>CUT
param28.does: How many octaves the LFO swings the cutoff, 0 to 3. Gives a wah-wah or breathing brightness at the LFO HZ rate. 0 is off.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param28.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Slow LFO HZ with LFO>CUT 1 sounds like a pad breathing.
param28.ask: What does LFO>CUT do to the sound?

param29.title: LFO>AMP
param29.does: Tremolo: the LFO makes the volume pulse, 0 to 100% deep. Slow is a gentle swell; fast is a shudder. 0 is off.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param29.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Keep it under 30% for a subtle shimmer.
param29.ask: What does LFO>AMP do to the sound?

param30.title: LFO>WID
param30.does: How much the LFO moves the square wave's WIDTH, 0 to 40%. It makes a moving, chorus-like tone, and only affects SQUARE waves.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param30.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Set WAVE A to SQUARE first.
param30.ask: What does LFO>WID do to the sound?

param31.title: GLIDE
param31.does: Portamento: how long the pitch takes to travel when you slide from one note to another, 0 to 2000 ms. Short is a quick snap; long is a slow, swooping slide. Tune's Glide speed scales every sound.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param31.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: 0 gives instant jumps without a slide.
param31.ask: What does GLIDE do to the sound?

param32.title: DRIVE
param32.does: Saturation squashes the wave: 0 is clean, low is warm, high is gritty and fuzzy. The Morph touch pad mapping adds drive live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param32.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Drive adds loudness; watch the Limit tag.
param32.ask: What does DRIVE do to the sound?

param33.title: CHORUS
param33.does: Chorus doubles the sound with a slightly detuned, wavering copy, so it sounds wider and shimmering. 0 is off, 100% is a thick swirl.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param33.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Chorus and reverb together sound big.
param33.ask: What does CHORUS do to the sound?

param34.title: DELAY
param34.does: Delay repeats the sound after a pause, 0 to 70%. Echo spacing follows the tempo: set it with DLY TIME. The X axis of the Space touch pad mapping adds delay live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param34.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Slow, sparse playing sounds best with echoes.
param34.ask: What does DELAY do to the sound?

param35.title: DLY TIME
param35.does: Chooses how long the echo waits, locked to the tempo: 1/16, 1/16 dotted, 1/8, 1/8 dotted or 1/4 note (one beat). Slower tempo means longer gaps.

use.text: Drag along the bar: it clicks through its steps; the name shows at the right.

param35.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: 1/8 dotted is the classic rhythmic echo.
param35.ask: What does DLY TIME do to the sound?

param36.title: DLY FB
param36.does: Feedback: how much of each echo is fed back in, 0 to 80%. Low gives one or two repeats; high gives a long trail that fades slowly.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param36.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Has no effect when DELAY is 0.
param36.ask: What does DLY FB do to the sound?

param37.title: REVERB
param37.does: Reverb adds the sense of a space, 0 to 80%. Low is a small room; high washes the sound out. The Y axis of the Space touch pad mapping adds reverb live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param37.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Pull this down if the sound feels washed out.
param37.ask: What does REVERB do to the sound?

param38.title: REV SIZE
param38.does: How big the room is, 20 to 98%: small is a quick tight tail; large is a long, drifting tail. Needs REVERB above 0 to be heard.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param38.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Large size with low REVERB is a subtle halo.
param38.ask: What does REV SIZE do to the sound?

param39.title: LEVEL
param39.does: A volume trim in decibels, about -34 dB to +12 dB, so different sounds sit at similar loudness. Random sounds set it for you. Master volume (System page) is separate.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param39.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: If the Limit tag shows, lower this or Master volume.
param39.ask: What does LEVEL do to the sound?

picosc.title: Oscillators picture
picosc.summary: One cycle of the tone, before the filter.
picosc.does: Drawn from the sound's own settings: wave A filled to its centre line, wave B dashed over it at its mix and pitch. FM bends A; SUB adds a deeper sine. It moves as you drag.

use.text: Nothing to tap. Drag WAVE, B MIX, B PITCH, WIDTH or FM and watch it change.

picosc.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 1/4. It only shows; it is not touchable.
tips: Two near-equal pitches make a slow beat: try DETUNE.
picosc.ask: What does the oscillators picture show?

picenv.title: Envelope picture
picenv.summary: How loud a note is, from press to fade.
picenv.does: Attack, decay, sustain, then release after the key is let go, on a square-root time scale so short attacks stay visible. Dotted rules mark the stage ends. A dot follows a note sounding now, roughly.

use.text: Nothing to tap. Drag ATTACK, DECAY, SUSTAIN or RELEASE and watch it change.

picenv.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. It only shows; it is not touchable.
tips: The dot is timed from when the screen saw the key go down.
picenv.ask: What does the envelope picture show?

picfilter.title: Filter picture
picfilter.summary: What the filter lets through, low to high.
picfilter.does: The filter's real response from 30 Hz to 16 kHz; the dot is the cutoff. The dashed curve is the cutoff at the top of the filter envelope (F.ENV).

use.text: Nothing to tap. Drag FILTER, CUTOFF, RESO or F.ENV and watch it change.

picfilter.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. It only shows; it is not touchable.
tips: Raise RESO for a peak at the dot; F.ENV opens the dashed curve.
picfilter.ask: What does the filter picture show?

sound-deep.recall: Sound tab, then All parameters. Prev and Next turn the four pages.

pulse.title: Pulse
pulse.intro: Eight pulse pads: clicks, metal, snaps, claps, pings, zaps, thumps and knocks. Pick a pad, shape it with four sliders, latch it, sync it, loop it.

tab_synth.title: PAGE TABS
tab_synth.summary: The strip of seven tabs along the top.
tab_synth.does: Synth, Sound, Pulse, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_synth.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all seven; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_synth.ask: What is on each of the pages?

pad0.title: PAD 1
pad0.summary: Plays pad 1 and selects it. Starts as click.
pad0.does: A short ringing click: TONE is its ring, LENGTH how fast it dies. Tap: it plays and is selected, so the picture and sliders show it. TYPE makes it any of the eight kinds. A latched pad shows LATCH: tap it to stop it.

use.text: Tap the pad: it plays, lights and is selected.
Press Q or U (two keys so both hands can play).
The small picture is the pad's real sound, drawn from its own generator.

pad0.recall: Pulse page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Pulse page; with Loop recording, taps go into the loop.
tips: Left / Right select the pad before or after without playing it.
pad0.ask: What can I do with pad 1?

pad1.title: PAD 2
pad1.summary: Plays pad 2 and selects it. Starts as metal.
pad1.does: Six square waves at clashing ratios in a high band, like a hi-hat. TONE is the lowest square. Tap: it plays and is selected. TYPE makes it any of the eight kinds. A latched pad shows LATCH: tap it to stop it.

use.text: Tap the pad: it plays, lights and is selected.
Press W or I (two keys so both hands can play).
The small picture is the pad's real sound, drawn from its own generator.

pad1.recall: Pulse page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Pulse page; with Loop recording, taps go into the loop.
tips: Left / Right select the pad before or after without playing it.
pad1.ask: What can I do with pad 2?

pad2.title: PAD 3
pad2.summary: Plays pad 3 and selects it. Starts as snap.
pad2.does: A short pitched body at TONE under a burst of bright noise, like a snare. Tap: it plays and is selected. TYPE makes it any of the eight kinds. A latched pad shows LATCH: tap it to stop it.

use.text: Tap the pad: it plays, lights and is selected.
Press E or O (two keys so both hands can play).
The small picture is the pad's real sound, drawn from its own generator.

pad2.recall: Pulse page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Pulse page; with Loop recording, taps go into the loop.
tips: Left / Right select the pad before or after without playing it.
pad2.ask: What can I do with pad 3?

pad3.title: PAD 4
pad3.summary: Plays pad 4 and selects it. Starts as FM ping.
pad3.does: A sine at TONE bent by another at 1.4 times it, fading fast: a glassy strike. Tap: it plays and is selected. TYPE makes it any of the eight kinds. A latched pad shows LATCH: tap it to stop it.

use.text: Tap the pad: it plays, lights and is selected.
Press R or P (two keys so both hands can play).
The small picture is the pad's real sound, drawn from its own generator.

pad3.recall: Pulse page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Pulse page; with Loop recording, taps go into the loop.
tips: Left / Right select the pad before or after without playing it.
pad3.ask: What can I do with pad 4?

pad4.title: PAD 5
pad4.summary: Plays pad 5 and selects it. Starts as clap.
pad4.does: Noise in a band at TONE, in three quick bursts 11 ms apart, then a tail. Tap: it plays and is selected. TYPE makes it any of the eight kinds. A latched pad shows LATCH: tap it to stop it.

use.text: Tap the pad: it plays, lights and is selected.
Press A or H (two keys so both hands can play).
The small picture is the pad's real sound, drawn from its own generator.

pad4.recall: Pulse page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Pulse page; with Loop recording, taps go into the loop.
tips: Left / Right select the pad before or after without playing it.
pad4.ask: What can I do with pad 5?

pad5.title: PAD 6
pad5.summary: Plays pad 6 and selects it. Starts as zap.
pad5.does: A sine that sweeps down from 25 times TONE to TONE: a laser-like drop. Tap: it plays and is selected. TYPE makes it any of the eight kinds. A latched pad shows LATCH: tap it to stop it.

use.text: Tap the pad: it plays, lights and is selected.
Press S or J (two keys so both hands can play).
The small picture is the pad's real sound, drawn from its own generator.

pad5.recall: Pulse page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Pulse page; with Loop recording, taps go into the loop.
tips: Left / Right select the pad before or after without playing it.
pad5.ask: What can I do with pad 6?

pad6.title: PAD 7
pad6.summary: Plays pad 7 and selects it. Starts as sub thump.
pad6.does: A low sine that drops from four times TONE to TONE in about 15 ms. Tap: it plays and is selected, so the picture and sliders show it. TYPE makes it any of the eight kinds. A latched pad shows LATCH: tap it to stop it.

use.text: Tap the pad: it plays, lights and is selected.
Press D or K (two keys so both hands can play).
The small picture is the pad's real sound, drawn from its own generator.

pad6.recall: Pulse page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Pulse page; with Loop recording, taps go into the loop.
tips: Left / Right select the pad before or after without playing it.
pad6.ask: What can I do with pad 7?

pad7.title: PAD 8
pad7.summary: Plays pad 8 and selects it. Starts as knock.
pad7.does: Two sine modes, TONE and 2.7 times TONE, struck: wood or a rim. Tap: it plays and is selected. TYPE makes it any of the eight kinds. A latched pad shows LATCH: tap it to stop it.

use.text: Tap the pad: it plays, lights and is selected.
Press F or L (two keys so both hands can play).
The small picture is the pad's real sound, drawn from its own generator.

pad7.recall: Pulse page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Pulse page; with Loop recording, taps go into the loop.
tips: Left / Right select the pad before or after without playing it.
pad7.ask: What can I do with pad 8?

pulsewave.title: SOUND PICTURE
pulsewave.summary: The selected pad's sound over its whole length.
pulsewave.does: Drawn by running the pad's own generator, the code the audio uses, so it is what you hear. Top left: its length. Top right: its tone, band or sweep. It redraws when a setting changes.

use.text: Nothing to press: move the sliders and watch it change.

pulsewave.recall: Pulse page, left of the sliders. Every kind is drawn over at least 24 samples.
tips: Level makes the picture taller or shorter: it is drawn to full scale.
pulsewave.ask: Why does the picture look like that?

pulsetone.title: TONE
pulsetone.summary: Hz: pitch, ring or band, by kind.
pulsetone.does: Pitch for FM ping, sub thump and zap (where they land), snap's body and knock's low mode. Ring for click. Band for clap; metal's squares start at it, their band 20 times higher. 20 Hz to 18 kHz.

use.text: Drag along the slider; it moves in octaves.

pulsetone.recall: Pulse page, first of the four sliders. It sets the selected pad only.
tips: Metal and snap brighten as TONE rises: their noise and squares follow it.
pulsetone.ask: What does TONE do on this kind of pad?

pulselength.title: LENGTH
pulselength.summary: How long one hit lasts, 1 ms to 2 s.
pulselength.does: The time from start to silence of one hit of the selected pad. Every kind fits its decay to it: a short length is a tight hit, a long one rings or sweeps out slowly.

use.text: Drag along the slider; it moves in octaves.

pulselength.recall: Pulse page, second slider. It sets the selected pad only.
tips: The picture's axis shows the length.
pulselength.ask: How long should a pad be?

pulserate.title: RATE
pulserate.summary: How often a latched pad is hit again.
pulserate.does: How often a latched pad is hit again, 0.25 to 200 Hz. With SYNC on it snaps to a division of the tempo, shown beside the value (1/16...).

use.text: Drag along the slider; it moves in octaves.

pulserate.recall: Pulse page, third slider. SYNC changes what it snaps to, not the value you set.
tips: Above about 20 Hz repeats stop being a rhythm and become a buzz.

pulselevel.title: LEVEL
pulselevel.does: How loud the selected pad is. Every pad has its own level; the master volume on the System page is on top of it. The picture is drawn to full scale, so it grows and shrinks with the level.

use.text: Drag along the slider.

tips: Pure tones sound louder than clicks at the same level.
pulselevel.ask: Why is one pad louder than the others?

pulselast.title: LAST 4 S
pulselast.summary: Every hit of the last four seconds, one lane a pad.
pulselast.does: One lane per pad, oldest on the left, now on the right. Each hit is a tick at the moment the engine played it, with a thin bar for its length.

use.text: Nothing to press: it is a display.

pulselast.recall: Pulse page, the strip above the soft keys. The selected pad's lane is a little brighter.
tips: Loop playback and latched pads show here too.
pulselast.ask: What is the strip showing me?

pulseloop.title: LOOP
pulseloop.summary: The loop pedal, here: pulse taps are recorded too.
pulseloop.does: The same loop pedal as Enter and the Synth page's Loop: count-in, record, play, overdub. Pad taps while it records go into the loop and play back with the pad's settings of the moment. Latched repeats are not recorded.

use.text: Tap to start the count-in, again to close the loop.
Enter does the same on every page.

pulseloop.recall: Pulse page, first soft key. Ctrl+U undoes a layer, Ctrl+D clears.
tips: Change a pad after recording and the loop plays the new sound.

pulselatch.title: LATCH
pulselatch.summary: The selected pad keeps going until you tap it again.
pulselatch.does: The selected pad is hit again RATE times a second until you stop it. Tap the pad, or Latch again, to stop it. Several pads can be latched at once; Backspace stops them all.

use.text: Select a pad, tap Latch; tap the pad to stop it.

pulselatch.recall: Pulse page, second soft key. Latches are not saved: nothing plays by itself at start.
tips: With SYNC on, a latched one-shot falls on the beat grid.
pulselatch.ask: How do I make a pad repeat?

pulsesync.title: SYNC
pulsesync.summary: Every pad's RATE follows the tempo.
pulsesync.does: On: each pad's rate snaps to the nearest division of the tempo (from 4 bars to 1/512), and latched one-shots land on the beat clock's grid, in time with the loop. Off: the rate is exactly the Hz you set.

use.text: Tap to switch it on or off.

pulsesync.recall: Pulse page, third soft key; the tempo is on the Tune page. It is saved with your settings.
tips: The RATE slider shows the division it snapped to.

pulsetype.title: TYPE
pulsetype.summary: The selected pad's kind: the next of eight.
pulsetype.does: Steps the selected pad through click, metal, snap, FM ping, clap, zap, sub thump and knock. The pad keeps its tone, length, rate and level; their meaning follows the new kind.

use.text: Tap until the kind you want; the label says the next one.

pulsetype.recall: Pulse page, last soft key. Any pad can be any kind, and two pads can be the same kind.
tips: Two pads of one kind with different tones make an interval.

backing.title: Backing
backing.intro: Backing chords from your key: pick what a chord tap does, how they play, and how long each lasts.

tab_synth.title: PAGE TABS
tab_synth.summary: The strip of seven tabs along the top.
tab_synth.does: Synth, Sound, Pulse, Backing, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_synth.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all seven; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_synth.ask: What is on each of the pages?

bmode0.title: PROGRESSION MODE
bmode0.summary: Chord taps build a looping progression.
bmode0.does: A chord tap adds to a looping sequence of up to eight chords. Tap Play (or the first chord) to hear it loop.

use.text: Tap chords in order to fill the strip.
Ctrl+B cycles the mode.

bmode0.recall: Backing page, top row; Synth page, mode button by the pads. Ctrl+B cycles Prog, Hold, Drone.
bmode0.ask: When would I use progression mode?

bmode1.title: HOLD MODE
bmode1.summary: Chord taps latch a single chord.
bmode1.does: A chord tap plays that one chord until you pick another. Tap the same chord again to stop it.

use.text: Tap a chord pad to latch it.
Ctrl+B cycles the mode.

bmode1.recall: Backing page, top row; Synth page, mode button by the pads. Ctrl+B cycles Prog, Hold, Drone.
bmode1.ask: When would I use hold mode?

bmode2.title: DRONE MODE
bmode2.summary: Chord taps latch a drone note.
bmode2.does: A chord tap switches a held bass note for that chord on or off. Several drones can sound at once.

use.text: Tap pads to add or remove drone notes.
Ctrl+B cycles the mode.

bmode2.recall: Backing page, top row; Synth page, mode button by the pads. Ctrl+B cycles Prog, Hold, Drone.
tips: A drone is the chord's root note, an octave up.
bmode2.ask: When would I use drone mode?

bstyle0.title: SUSTAIN STYLE
bstyle0.summary: Chord notes ring continuously, gliding to the next chord.
bstyle0.does: All notes of the chord are held for the whole chord length; when the chord changes the notes slide to the new ones. The calmest style, good under slow playing.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle0.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
bstyle0.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bstyle1.title: PULSE STYLE
bstyle1.summary: The chord re-strikes on every beat.
bstyle1.does: The root is held while the upper notes of the chord are struck short on every beat, like a steady organ or guitar chop.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle1.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
bstyle1.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bstyle2.title: ARP UP STYLE
bstyle2.summary: Chord notes play one by one, upward.
bstyle2.does: An arpeggio: the chord's notes are played one at a time, climbing across two octaves and starting over. Speed is set by steps per beat.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle2.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
tips: Arp steps per beat is the stepper below.
bstyle2.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bstyle3.title: ARP DOWN STYLE
bstyle3.summary: Chord notes play one by one, downward.
bstyle3.does: An arpeggio running downward through the chord's notes across two octaves, then starting again. Speed is steps per beat.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle3.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
tips: Arp steps per beat is the stepper below.
bstyle3.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bstyle4.title: ARP UP-DN STYLE
bstyle4.summary: Chord notes climb then fall, back and forth.
bstyle4.does: An arpeggio that climbs to the top of the two-octave span, turns round and falls back down, repeating. Speed is steps per beat.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle4.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
tips: Arp steps per beat is the stepper below.
bstyle4.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bslot0.title: PROGRESSION SLOTS
bslot0.summary: The chords you queued, up to eight. Tap to select one.
bslot0.does: Each filled slot shows a chord name; the playing one is inverted. Tap a slot to select it (double frame), then tap a chord pad to replace it. Tap the selected slot again to deselect.

use.text: Tap a filled slot, then a chord pad to swap it.

bslot0.recall: Backing page, progression row; also Synth page. Ctrl+Backspace removes the last chord.
tips: Empty slots show only their number and cannot be tapped.
bslot0.ask: How do I change one chord in my progression?

bremove.title: REMOVE LAST
bremove.summary: Takes the last chord off the progression.
bremove.does: Deletes the last chord in the queue, one per tap. The rest keep playing. Does not touch the held chord or drones.

use.text: Tap Remove last.
Ctrl+Backspace.

bremove.recall: Backing page, first row of buttons. Ctrl+Backspace. To replace instead, tap a slot then a chord.
bremove.ask: How do I drop the last chord I added?

bclear.title: CLEAR ALL
bclear.does: Removes every chord, the held chord and all drones, and stops the backing. Does not touch the loop or the pulse pads.

use.text: Tap Clear all.

bclear.recall: Backing page only; it has no key. No undo: tap the chords again.
bclear.ask: How do I start the backing chords over?

bseventh.title: 7TH CHORDS
bseventh.does: Off: three-note triads. On: four-note seventh chords, which sound richer and more jazzy. Pad names update to match. Applies to everything the backing plays.

use.text: Tap to switch; inverted means on.

bseventh.recall: Backing page, third button. Tap again to go back to triads.
bseventh.ask: What does 7th chords change in the sound?

bmetro.title: METRONOME
bmetro.does: Plays a quiet click in time with the tempo, louder on the first beat of each bar. The count-in click always sounds regardless.

use.text: Tap to switch; also Click on the Tune page.
Ctrl+M.

bmetro.recall: Backing page and Tune page (Click); Ctrl+M. It is one shared setting.
bmetro.ask: How do I turn the click on?

chord0.title: CHORD PADS I-VII
chord0.summary: The seven chords of your key; what a tap does depends on mode.
chord0.does: Each pad shows a chord and its numeral (small = minor). Prog: a tap adds it to a looping progression of up to eight. Hold: latches one chord. Drone: toggles its root as a held note.

use.text: Tap a pad. Mode: the button beside the pads.
Alt+Z..M: chords I to VII.

chord0.recall: Synth and Backing pages. Clear all on the Backing page clears; Ctrl+Backspace removes the last chord.
tips: Chords follow the key and scale.
chord0.ask: What do the chord pads do in each mode?

backmode.title: CHORD MODE
backmode.summary: Prog, Hold or Drone: what a chord tap does.
backmode.does: Prog adds taps to a looping progression. Hold plays one chord until you pick another (tap it again to stop). Drone switches a held bass note for each chord you tap on and off.

use.text: Tap to step Prog, Hold, Drone.
Ctrl+B steps the mode.

backmode.recall: Synth page, beside the pads; three buttons on the Backing page. Ctrl+B steps it.
tips: Mode names appear as a toast when you use Ctrl+B.
backmode.ask: What is the difference between Prog, Hold and Drone?

backplay.title: BACKING PLAY / STOP
backplay.summary: Starts and stops the backing chords.
backplay.does: Plays the progression (or held chord or drones) in time with the tempo, on the chord length set in Backing. Tapping a chord in Prog mode already starts it, so Play then stops it.

use.text: Tap to start or stop; inverted while playing.
Ctrl+Space toggles it from any page.

backplay.recall: Synth page and Backing page, beside the chord pads. Ctrl+Space.
tips: Backing joins the bar in progress if a loop or synced pulses are already running.
backplay.ask: Why does the backing start when I tap a chord?

chordbeats-.title: BEATS PER CHORD
chordbeats-.summary: How long each chord lasts, in beats.
chordbeats-.does: From 1 to 8 beats; 4 is one bar of 4/4. Shorter means the progression moves faster. Changes how long each slot plays and when arpeggios turn over.

use.text: Tap − or +.

chordbeats-.recall: Backing page, left of the second row of steppers. Default 4.
chordbeats-.ask: How do I make the chords change faster?

arprate-.title: ARP STEPS PER BEAT
arprate-.does: How many notes an arpeggio plays per beat, 1 to 4. At 2 you hear eighth notes. It only changes the Arp styles; Sustain and Pulse ignore it.

use.text: Tap − or +.

arprate-.recall: Backing page, right of Beats per chord. Default 2.
tips: Pulse always plays once per beat, whatever this says.
arprate-.ask: How do I speed up the arpeggio?

bpm2-.title: TEMPO
bpm2-.summary: The tempo in beats per minute.
bpm2-.does: Sets the speed of the backing, the loop and the pulse pads' SYNC together: 40 to 240 bpm, 1 per tap. It is the same setting as on the Tune page.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Ctrl+T taps a tempo.

bpm2-.recall: Backing page, below the progression; also the Tune page. Ctrl+T.
bpm2-.ask: How do I change the tempo?

backvol.title: BACKING VOLUME
backvol.summary: How loud the backing chords are.
backvol.does: The chords' level, 0 to 100%, separate from the lead and loop. Master volume on System sets the overall level.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar.

backvol.recall: Backing page, right of Tempo. Loop and master volumes are on System.
backvol.ask: How do I make the backing quieter than my lead?

bresync.title: USE CURRENT LEAD SOUND
bresync.summary: Makes the backing play the lead's sound.
bresync.does: The backing keeps the sound it started with, so you can change the lead freely. Tap this when you want the chords to use the sound you are playing now. The line inside shows both names.

use.text: Tap the wide button.

bresync.recall: Backing page, full-width button. The backing otherwise keeps its old sound until cleared and restarted.
bresync.ask: Why does the backing not change when I change my sound?

backing.recall: Backing tab. On Synth the Prog and Play buttons are the same chord controls.

tune.title: Tune
tune.intro: Key, scale, octave, tempo and slide speed: the settings that make everything you play fit together. Listen can guess a song's key.

tab_synth.title: PAGE TABS
tab_synth.summary: The strip of seven tabs along the top.
tab_synth.does: Synth, Sound, Pulse, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_synth.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all seven; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_synth.ask: What is on each of the pages?

root0.title: KEY (ROOT NOTE)
root0.summary: Pick the home note of your key: C to B.
root0.does: The root is the note the scale is built on and the one the strings return to. Changing it moves every string, chord pad and the bright root frames. All three strings stay locked to the scale.

use.text: Tap one of the twelve notes; the active one is inverted.
Ctrl+K steps up a semitone (Shift added: down).

root0.recall: Tune page, top block; Synth header shows it. Ctrl+K steps up, Ctrl+Shift+K down. Listen can set it too.
tips: The chord pads follow the new key straight away.
root0.ask: How do I choose the right key to play along with a song?

scale0.title: MAJOR
scale0.does: The classic bright scale. Seven notes per octave, so strings have more to choose from and some pairs clash a little if you slide through them.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale0.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

scale1.title: NATURAL MINOR
scale1.does: The standard minor scale: sad, moody, cinematic. Same notes as the major scale that starts a minor third higher.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale1.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.
scale1.ask: When should I use natural minor?

scale2.title: MAJOR PENTATONIC
scale2.summary: Five notes: sweet, hard to get wrong.
scale2.does: Five notes per octave with no tense steps, so almost anything you play sounds pleasant. Country, folk and pop melodies.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale2.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.
scale2.ask: When should I use major pentatonic?

scale3.title: MINOR PENTATONIC
scale3.summary: Five notes: bluesy and rocky. The default.
scale3.does: Five notes of the minor scale with the awkward ones left out. The default scale (A minor pentatonic): good for riffs and solos.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale3.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.
tips: The scale decides which notes the keys give: nothing you press is wrong.
scale3.ask: When should I use minor pentatonic?

scale4.title: BLUES
scale4.summary: Six notes: minor pentatonic plus a blue note.
scale4.does: Adds one gritty in-between note to the minor pentatonic. Sliding through it gives the blues sound.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale4.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

scale5.title: DORIAN
scale5.summary: Seven notes: minor, with a brighter sixth.
scale5.does: A minor-sounding scale with a lifted sixth note: jazzy, folky, hopeful rather than sad.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale5.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

scale6.title: MIXOLYDIAN
scale6.summary: Seven notes: major with a flat seventh.
scale6.does: A major-sounding scale with a lowered seventh: relaxed, bluesy-major, a rock and funk favourite.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale6.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

scale7.title: CHROMATIC
scale7.does: Every semitone, so every key is a half-step from the next and nothing is locked. Notes can clash. Chord pads still use the major scale's chords.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale7.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

oct-.title: OCTAVE
oct-.summary: Moves the whole instrument up or down in octaves.
oct-.does: Each step shifts every string by 12 semitones, from -3 to +3. Held notes sweep to the new octave without restarting.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Down / Up arrows, or - and =.

oct-.recall: Tune page and Synth page bottom row. Arrows are on the Q20 symbol layer.
oct-.ask: Why do all my notes sound an octave off?

rowint-.title: STRING GAP
rowint-.summary: How far apart the three strings are tuned.
rowint-.does: Semitones between neighbouring strings, 1 to 12 (default 5, a fourth, like a bass or guitar). Lower overlaps the strings; 12 makes each string an octave apart. A semitone is the smallest step on a keyboard.

use.text: Tap − or +.

rowint-.recall: Tune page, middle of the first stepper row. Default 5.
tips: Smaller gaps make chord shapes easier to finger.

bendr-.title: BEND RANGE
bendr-.summary: How far the bend keys move the pitch.
bendr-.does: Holding Left or Right bends the pitch down or up by up to this many semitones (1 to 12, default 2) with a short ramp. Also the reach of the Bend touch pad mapping's left-right axis.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Hold Left / Right (or [ ]) to bend.

bendr-.recall: Tune page, third stepper of the first row. Default 2.
tips: 12 gives a full octave of bend.
bendr-.ask: How do I get a bigger pitch bend?

bpm-.title: TEMPO
bpm-.summary: The tempo in beats per minute (bpm).
bpm-.does: Sets the speed of the loop and the pulse pads' SYNC: 40 to 240 bpm, one per tap here. Delay times and the metronome follow it.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Ctrl+T: tap in time.

bpm-.recall: Tune page. Ctrl+T taps a tempo; the Pulse page's SYNC follows it.
bpm-.ask: How do I match the tempo of a song?

tap.title: TAP
tap.summary: Sets the tempo by tapping it.
tap.does: Tap in time a few times: it averages your last six taps (a pause over two seconds starts afresh) and sets the tempo to match. At least two taps are needed.

use.text: Tap steadily on the button.
Ctrl+T from any page.

tap.recall: Tune page, middle of the tempo row. Ctrl+T works anywhere. Fix errors with the Tempo stepper.

metro.title: CLICK
metro.summary: The metronome: a click on every beat.
metro.does: A soft click in time with the tempo, accented on beat one of each bar. Loop count-ins click regardless.

use.text: Tap to switch on or off; inverted means on.
Ctrl+M.

metro.ask: How do I play along with a click?

glidescale.title: GLIDE SPEED
glidescale.summary: Makes every slide faster or slower.
glidescale.does: A multiplier on each sound's own glide time (how long slides take): all the way left is instant jumps, the default is x1.00, and the far right is four times slower. It affects all sounds at once.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar. Left reads instant.

glidescale.recall: Tune page, right of Tap and Click. Default is x1.00 (a quarter of the way along).
tips: A sound's own GLIDE (Sound > All parameters) is the starting point.
glidescale.ask: How do I make slides snappier or slower?

listen.title: LISTEN
listen.summary: Listens for six seconds and guesses key and tempo.
listen.does: Records from the system's default audio input, then estimates the key and tempo of music playing nearby, with a likely/guess/unsure rating. This Hackberry has no microphone, so it will say so.

use.text: Tap Listen and hold the source near the mic.

listen.recall: Tune page, Listen box at the bottom. Nothing changes until you tap Use key, Use tempo or Use both.
tips: Always check the result by ear: detection is an estimate.
listen.ask: What does Listen need to work?

lkey.title: USE KEY
lkey.does: Sets the key's root note and switches to major or minor to match. If you were on a pentatonic scale it stays pentatonic (major or minor). Tempo is not touched.

use.text: Tap Use key after a result appears.

lkey.recall: Tune page, after Listen returns a result. Change it back in the Key and Scale blocks.

ltempo.title: USE TEMPO
ltempo.does: Sets the tempo to the detected bpm, if a pulse was found. The key and scale are left alone.

use.text: Tap Use tempo after a result appears.

ltempo.recall: Tune page, after Listen returns a result. Fix by hand with Tempo or Tap.

lboth.title: USE BOTH
lboth.summary: Applies both the key and the tempo.
lboth.does: Does Use key and Use tempo together in one tap, so you can play along with what you just listened to.

use.text: Tap Use both after a result appears.

lboth.recall: Tune page, after Listen returns a result. Undo by choosing the key, scale and tempo by hand.
lboth.ask: Should I use both the key and tempo?

lnext.title: OTHER KEY
lnext.summary: Shows Listen's next best key guess.
lnext.does: Listen keeps its three best key guesses; the first is the most likely. Tap to cycle through guess 1, 2 and 3, then Use key applies the one shown.

use.text: Tap to step to the next guess.

lnext.recall: Tune page, after Listen returns a result. The button says which guess (1 of 3) is shown.
tips: The second and third guesses are rated half as sure.
lnext.ask: What if Listen picks the wrong key?

tune.recall: Tune tab, or tap the key, tempo or octave readout at the top of Synth.

system.title: System
