system.intro: Master volume, touch pad mapping, recording and saving, key test, device status, and Panic.

tab_synth.title: PAGE TABS
tab_synth.summary: The strip of seven tabs along the top.
tab_synth.does: Synth, Sound, Pulse, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_synth.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all seven; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_synth.ask: What is on each of the pages?

volume.title: MASTER VOLUME
volume.does: Sets the final loudness of everything, 0 to 100%. A limiter means the output can never exceed full scale, but a Limit tag shows when it is holding sound back.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar.

volume.recall: System page, top left. Each pulse pad and the loop have their own level too.
tips: If the sound is distorted or quiet with Limit showing, lower this.
volume.ask: Why is it quiet, or why does Limit show?

loopvol.title: LOOP VOLUME
loopvol.summary: How loud the recorded loop is.
loopvol.does: Level of the loop pedal's layers, 0 to 100%, separate from what you play live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar.

loopvol.recall: System page, top right. Loop pedal itself is on the Synth page.
loopvol.ask: How do I balance the loop against my playing?

xymap0.title: FILTER MAPPING
xymap0.summary: Touch pad pair: Cutoff and resonance.
xymap0.does: X is cutoff (dark to bright), Y is resonance (a whistling edge). Drag to sweep the filter like a classic synth knob pair.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap0.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap0.ask: What does the filter mapping do?

xymap1.title: WOBBLE MAPPING
xymap1.summary: Touch pad pair: Cutoff and vibrato.
xymap1.does: X is cutoff, Y adds vibrato (pitch wobble). Drag up for a wobble, sideways to open or close the sound.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap1.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap1.ask: What does the wobble mapping do?

xymap2.title: MORPH MAPPING
xymap2.summary: Touch pad pair: Timbre and drive.
xymap2.does: X blends in the second oscillator (timbre, the tone colour), Y adds drive (distortion). Moves the sound from plain to rich and gritty.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap2.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap2.ask: What does the morph mapping do?

xymap3.title: SPACE MAPPING
xymap3.summary: Touch pad pair: Delay and reverb.
xymap3.does: X adds echoes (delay), Y adds room sound (reverb). Makes the sound drift away to the right and upward.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap3.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap3.ask: What does the space mapping do?

xymap4.title: BEND MAPPING
xymap4.summary: Touch pad pair: Pitch and cutoff.
xymap4.does: X bends pitch down or up (by the Bend range), Y moves cutoff. Centre is no bend. Good for dive bombs and rising wails.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap4.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap4.ask: What does the bend mapping do?

xymap5.title: GLITCH MAPPING
xymap5.summary: Touch pad pair: Coarse and grit.
xymap5.does: Crushes everything you hear into a rough digital sound: X is coarse (blockier, metallic), Y is grit (rougher, noisier). Coloured streaks trail the wave.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap5.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
tips: Glitch affects lead, chord pads, loop and pulses together.
xymap5.ask: What does the glitch mapping do?

xyhold2.title: HOLD
xyhold2.summary: Keeps the pad's last position after you lift.
xyhold2.does: Off: the sound returns to normal on release. On: the touch pad's last position stays applied until you turn Hold off or touch the pad again. Same switch as on the Synth page's scope.

use.text: Tap to switch; inverted means on.

xyhold2.recall: System page, end of the mapping row; Synth page scope corner.
xyhold2.ask: Why does my touch pad effect stay on?

chordrow.title: CHORD ROW
chordrow.summary: The bottom letter row plays chords, not notes.
chordrow.does: On: Z to M play the chord pads I to VII instead of the low string, and labels show on those keys. Off: it is a string again. The Alt key does the same while held.

use.text: Tap to switch; inverted means on.
$ toggles it; hold Alt + Z..M for a single chord.

chordrow.recall: System page, first button below the mapping row. $ toggles it; the toast says which state.
tips: The Pulse page keeps the bottom row as the low string.
chordrow.ask: How do I play chords from the keyboard?

recwav.title: RECORD
recwav.summary: Records what you hear to a WAV file.
recwav.does: Starts recording the full output (lead, chord pads, loop, pulses) into a WAV audio file in recordings/. Press again to stop; the file name shows. A REC timer blinks on the Synth page.

use.text: Tap Record, play, then tap Stop rec.
Ctrl+E starts and stops.

recwav.recall: System page; Ctrl+E anywhere. Files are in ~/vrequency/recordings/. Play last plays the newest.
tips: Recording runs in real time: play the take you want to keep.
recwav.ask: How do I record a take?

playlast.title: PLAY LAST
playlast.summary: Plays your newest recording through the speaker.
playlast.does: Plays the most recent file in recordings/ with the system player (pw-play or aplay). The same button stops it. You can play along while it runs. It cannot choose older files.

use.text: Tap Play last; tap again to stop.
Ctrl+W.

playlast.ask: How do I hear my last recording?

savesession.title: SAVE SESSION
savesession.summary: Saves the whole setup as a session file.
savesession.does: Writes your sounds, key, tempo, backing, loop and the pulse pads into a timestamped file in sessions/. It does not stop anything. The list below shows the four newest.

use.text: Tap Save session; a toast shows the file name.

savesession.recall: System page. Load from the list below the buttons, then press play on the loop.
tips: Quitting saves your setup automatically; sessions are for keeping versions.

keytest.title: KEY TEST
keytest.summary: Shows which keys the keyboard reports.
keytest.does: Opens a panel that lists every key you hold and the most you held at once. Use it to check that the keyboard can read several keys together (chords) without ghosting, which is a hardware limit.

use.text: Tap Key test to open; Close (or Esc) to leave.

keytest.recall: System page, last button of the row. Esc also closes it and goes to Synth.
keytest.ask: How many keys can my keyboard read at once?

session0.title: SAVED SESSIONS
session0.summary: Your four newest sessions. Tap to load one.
session0.does: Loads that session: sounds, key, tempo, backing, loop and the pulse pads replace what you have. Sounds do not start by themselves; press play on the loop or the backing, or tap a chord.

use.text: Tap a session name. A toast confirms.

session0.recall: System page, Saved sessions. Only the four newest show. Save first if you want to keep your current setup.
tips: Sessions saved by older versions load too; their track, beat and drum kit are left out.
session0.ask: What happens when I load a session?

panic.title: PANIC
panic.does: Silences all notes and stops the chord pads, latched pulses and loop playback. Clears Glitch and sustain. A loop being recorded is dropped; a finished loop is kept. Use it when a note sticks.

use.text: Tap Panic.
Backspace from any page.

panic.recall: System page, bottom left; Backspace anywhere.
panic.ask: A note is stuck. How do I stop everything?

latency-.title: LOOP FIX
latency-.summary: Moves recorded loops earlier or later.
latency-.does: Milliseconds, 0 to 500 in steps of 10. Bluetooth speakers play about 0.2 s behind your fingers, so your recording lands late; this shifts recorded hits earlier to match. Raise it if hits land late, lower it if early.

use.text: Tap − or +, record a bar and listen.

latency-.recall: System page, bottom row. Set to 200 automatically for Bluetooth outputs; 0 for others.
tips: Live playing keeps its delay; only recordings are corrected.
latency-.ask: My loops play late. How do I fix the timing?

factory.title: FACTORY SOUNDS
factory.summary: Restores slots 1-0 and the dream sounds.
factory.does: Puts the ten original sounds back in the slots, replacing anything you stored, and re-adds any of the five dream sounds you deleted. Your own favourites stay.

use.text: Tap Factory sounds. A toast reports what returned.

factory.recall: System page, bottom row. This overwrites slots 1-0 and cannot be undone.
factory.ask: How do I get the original sounds back?

quit.title: QUIT
quit.summary: Saves your setup and closes the app.
quit.does: Quits venv-vrequency. Your sounds, key, tempo, settings and pulse pads are saved first and come back next time.

use.text: Tap Quit.
Ctrl+Q.

quit.recall: System page, bottom right; Ctrl+Q anywhere. Reopen from the app grid.

system.recall: System tab. Ctrl+E records what you hear; Ctrl+W plays the last recording.

key-test.title: Key test
key-test.intro: A panel over the System page that shows live which keys the keyboard reports, and how many it reads at once.

keytestclose.title: CLOSE KEY TEST
keytestclose.does: The panel lists the keys held now, the most held at once, and the last twelve down and up events. A key you did not press showing up, or a pressed key missing, is a keyboard limit, not a synth fault.

use.text: Tap Close.
Esc closes it and returns to Synth.

keytestclose.recall: Open from System page, Key test. Hold one key on each row then add more to find the limit.
tips: Most keys held at once is the number to report.
keytestclose.ask: What am I supposed to look for in Key test?

key-test.recall: System tab, Key test button. Close or Esc leaves it.

help.title: Help
help.intro: The key lists built into the app: three pages for playing, commands and the pulse pads. The list follows your keymap.

tab_synth.title: PAGE TABS
tab_synth.summary: The strip of seven tabs along the top.
tab_synth.does: Synth, Sound, Pulse, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_synth.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all seven; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_synth.ask: What is on each of the pages?

help_next.title: HELP PAGE BUTTON
help_next.summary: Cycles through the three key lists.
help_next.does: The Help page lists keys in three pages: Playing, Commands (hold Ctrl), and Pulse and recording. Each tap moves on to the next page, then wraps back to Playing.

use.text: Tap to step to the next list.

help_next.recall: Help tab, bottom left. Ctrl+H opens Help from any page and closes it again.
tips: The bindings shown follow your keymap.json.
help_next.ask: Where do I find every keyboard shortcut?

help_back.title: BACK TO PLAYING
help_back.does: Leaves Help and goes straight to the instrument. Esc does the same from any page.

use.text: Tap Back to playing.
Esc, or Ctrl+H to close Help.

help_back.ask: How do I get back to the instrument?

help_section.title: SECTION TITLE
help_section.summary: Names which of the three key lists you are reading.
help_section.does: Help has three lists: Playing, Commands, and Pulse and recording. The title says which one is open; Next steps to the following list.

use.text: Read only. Use the Next button to change list.

help_section.recall: Top left of the Help page.
help_section.ask: Which key list should I read first?

help_tour.title: TOUR
help_tour.summary: Opens this tour: a picture of every page you can tap.
help_tour.does: Starts the interactive tour. It never changes your sound or settings; it only draws pictures and reads help cards. Tap a control to read what it does.

use.text: Tap Tour. Then tap any control in the picture.
Ctrl+O opens the tour from any page; Esc leaves it.

help_tour.recall: Help page, top row. Or Ctrl+O from any page, or ask Rook to show you.
tips: The tour remembers the page you were on last.
help_tour.ask: Can you show me around the app?

help_ask.title: ASK ROOK
help_ask.summary: Opens a chat with Rook, ready to ask about this guide.
help_ask.does: Opens the chat dock with a question started for you. Rook can answer here and point at controls on the screen.

use.text: Tap it, or tap any key row to ask about that row.
Ctrl+Y opens the chat dock on any page.

help_ask.recall: Help page, top right. Ctrl+Y from any page.
tips: Esc hands the keys back to the page.
help_ask.ask: Who is Rook and what can they do?

help.recall: Help tab, or Ctrl+H from anywhere. Ctrl+H again leaves it.

chat.title: Chat
chat.intro: Talk with the AI copilot connected to the app. It can play, change sounds and shape pulse pads while you chat.

tab_synth.title: PAGE TABS
tab_synth.summary: The strip of seven tabs along the top.
tab_synth.does: Synth, Sound, Pulse, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_synth.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all seven; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_synth.ask: What is on each of the pages?

chat_history.title: CHAT HISTORY
chat_history.does: Messages from the copilot (white name tag) and from you (outlined YOU). A ? after a name means it is asking you something; tip marks a suggestion. The top right says whether a copilot is listening. The last 200 are kept.

use.text: Drag up or down to scroll.
Up / Down (or PageUp / PageDown) scroll.

chat_history.recall: Chat tab; Ctrl+Y jumps here from any page and back. Esc leaves.
tips: New messages on other pages appear in a strip at the bottom for a few seconds.
chat_history.ask: How does the copilot see what I am playing?

chat_send.title: SEND
chat_send.does: Sends the text in the box to the copilot. On this page letters type instead of playing strings; Enter sends, Backspace deletes. Messages wait for a copilot if none is connected.

use.text: Tap Send.
Enter sends; Backspace deletes a letter.

chat_send.recall: Chat tab, bottom right. Ctrl+Y toggles the page; Tab and Ctrl shortcuts still work.
tips: Hold Shift for capital letters; the symbol layer gives digits and punctuation.
chat_send.ask: How do I type to the copilot?

chat_input.title: MESSAGE BOX
chat_input.summary: Where your message to Rook appears as you type.
chat_input.does: On this page the letter keys type instead of playing. Enter sends; Backspace edits. A cursor blinks while you can type. Messages carry where you were when you sent them.

use.text: Just type, then press Enter to send.
Tap Send to send; the keyboard does the typing.

chat_input.recall: Chat tab, bottom. Ctrl+Shift+Y jumps here from any page.
tips: Esc leaves the page and plays again.
chat_input.ask: What can I ask you to do?

chat.recall: Chat tab, or Ctrl+Shift+Y from anywhere. Ctrl+Y opens a small chat dock instead.

recall.title: RECALL
recall.summary: How to get back to anything you changed.
recall.does: Every card ends with a Recall line: where the control lives, its shortcut, and how to undo or reset it. Sounds come back from slots (1-0), favourites or Ctrl+Z; setups from sessions; a stuck mess from Panic.

use.text: Read the Recall line on any card to find the page and shortcut.
Ctrl+Z undoes the last sound change; Backspace is Panic.
Tap a slot or favourite to bring a sound back; System lists sessions.

recall.recall: Help tab, Ctrl+H, lists every key. Esc returns to Synth from anywhere.
tips: Not everything is undoable: Store to a slot and Delete are final.
recall.ask: How do I get back a sound or setting I lost?

scale-lock.title: SCALE LOCK
scale-lock.summary: Every key plays a note that fits the key and scale.
scale-lock.does: You pick a root note and a scale (a set of notes that sound good together). The strings only offer those notes, so nothing is a wrong note. Left to right goes up the scale. Hold Shift for chromatic: every semitone, off the scale.

use.text: Tune page: tap a root note, then a scale.
Ctrl+K key up, Ctrl+S next scale, hold Shift for semitones.

scale-lock.recall: Tune page, Key and Scale; header on the Synth page shows both. Default is A minor pentatonic.
tips: Pentatonic scales have five notes and are the hardest to get wrong.
scale-lock.ask: Why can I not play a wrong note?

strings.title: THE THREE STRINGS
strings.summary: Each letter row is a string that plays one note at a time.
strings.does: High string Q to P, middle A to L, low Z to M. Each is monophonic: one note at a time, like a real string. The strings are tuned a gap apart (5 semitones by default) so shapes across rows make chords.

use.text: Press a letter; hold shapes across rows for chords.
Press a note; drag to slide.

strings.recall: Synth page, the three strings. Tune page, String gap changes the spacing.
tips: Shapes across the rows make chords without the chord pads.
strings.ask: How are the three strings laid out?

slides.title: SLIDES (GLIDE)
slides.summary: A second key on a held string slides the note.
slides.does: Hold one key and press another on the same row: the pitch glides to the new note without restarting (no new attack). Release the newer key and it glides back. The glide time is the sound's GLIDE setting times Tune's Glide speed.

use.text: Hold A, press F, release F.
Press a note on the string and drag sideways.
Hold a shape across rows and re-finger it: the chord glides.

slides.recall: Synth page strings. Slide time: Tune > Glide speed, or Sound > All parameters > GLIDE.
tips: Sustain makes slides smoother: new keys slide the ringing note.
slides.ask: How do I make the note slide?

loop-pedal.title: LOOP PEDAL FLOW
loop-pedal.summary: One button: count in, record, play, layer.
loop-pedal.does: 1 Tap Loop: count-in. 2 Play: it records notes, slides, bends and pad moves. 3 Tap: recording ends at the bar's end, then it loops. 4 Tap: add a layer (DUB). 5 Tap: finish it. Up to six layers, 64 bars; each layer keeps its sound.

use.text: Tap Loop; the label always says what the next tap does.
Enter; Ctrl+U undo layer, Ctrl+L play/stop, Ctrl+D clear.

loop-pedal.recall: Synth page, bottom left. Loop volume: System. Loops late? System > Loop fix.
tips: The loop records notes, not audio, so it follows tempo changes.
loop-pedal.ask: How do I record my first loop?

bar-lines.title: BAR LINES AND QUANTISE
bar-lines.summary: Things start and change on the bar so they stay in time.
bar-lines.does: A bar is a group of beats (4 here). Recorded loops end on a bar, and with SYNC latched pulse pads fall on the same beat grid.

use.text: Start things in any order: they join the bar in progress.

bar-lines.recall: Tempo: Tune page. Bluetooth timing: System > Loop fix. Metronome: Ctrl+M.
tips: Metronome: Ctrl+M, or Click on the Tune page.
bar-lines.ask: Why do things wait for the next bar?

sessions-favourites-state.title: SESSIONS, FAVOURITES, SETUP
sessions-favourites-state.summary: Three ways your work is kept.
sessions-favourites-state.does: Your setup (slots, key, tempo, settings, pulse pads) saves itself on quit. A favourite is one saved sound. A session is a snapshot: sounds, key, tempo, backing, loop and the pulse pads.

use.text: Sound page: Save. System page: Save session, tap one to load.
Ctrl+F saves a favourite.

sessions-favourites-state.recall: Files live in ~/vrequency/: state.json, favourites/, sessions/, recordings/. Delete keymap.json to reset keys.
tips: Sessions list shows the four newest.
sessions-favourites-state.ask: What is the difference between a favourite, a session and my setup?

command-layer.title: COMMAND LAYER (CTRL)
command-layer.summary: Hold Ctrl and press a letter for a command instead of a note.
command-layer.does: Ctrl is the command key. Held, letters run actions: R new sound, N mutate, Z undo, F favourite, K key up, S scale, T tap tempo, M click, G pad mapping, E record, W play last, H help, Y chat, Q quit.

use.text: Hold Ctrl, press the letter. Shift reverses K and S.

command-layer.recall: Help tab, Commands page lists them all. Edit keymap.json to rebind; delete it to reset.
tips: Ctrl+V switches the scope's 3D view; hold Ctrl+C or Ctrl+X to sweep the filter.

q20-layers.title: Q20 KEYBOARD LAYERS
q20-layers.summary: Arrows and digits sit on the Q20's symbol and number layers.
q20-layers.does: The Q20 keyboard puts digits (1-9, 0 pick sounds) on a number layer and arrows (bend, octave) on a symbol layer. [ ] also bend and - = also change octave. Alt is the chord layer, Ctrl the command layer, $ toggles chord row.

use.text: Use the layer key, then the digit or arrow.
Backspace is Panic, Enter the loop pedal, Tab next page, Esc home.

q20-layers.recall: Help tab shows the keys. System > Key test shows exactly what the keyboard reports.
tips: Key test is the way to check which keys reach the app.
q20-layers.ask: Where are the arrow keys and numbers on the Q20?

xy-mappings.title: TOUCH PAD MAPPINGS
xy-mappings.summary: Six pairs of controls for the scope pad.
xy-mappings.does: Filter: cutoff and reso. Wobble: cutoff and vibrato. Morph: timbre and drive. Space: delay and reverb. Bend: pitch and cutoff. Glitch: coarse and grit (crushes everything). X is left-right, Y is bottom-top.

use.text: Drag on the scope; pick the pair with the corner button.
Ctrl+G steps through them.

xy-mappings.recall: Synth page scope corner; System page row of six. Hold keeps the position.
tips: Moves are recorded into the loop while it records.
xy-mappings.ask: Which touch pad mapping should I use?

glitch.title: GLITCH
glitch.summary: Crushes everything you hear into a rough digital sound.
glitch.does: While your finger is on the pad (or Hold is on) lead, chord pads, loop and pulses are crushed into a blocky, lo-fi sound. Right is coarser, up is rougher. Streaks trail the scope wave. Lift to restore; Backspace clears it.

use.text: Choose Glitch, drag on the scope.
Backspace switches it off.

glitch.recall: Synth page scope corner, or System page, Glitch. Lift your finger to end it.
glitch.ask: What does Glitch do to my sound?

chord-modes.title: CHORD PAD MODES
chord-modes.summary: What a chord tap does: Hold or Drone.
chord-modes.does: Hold plays one chord until you pick another or tap it again. Drone switches held bass notes on and off, one per chord. The pads take the sound that is live when they start.

use.text: Tap the mode button beside the chord pads.
Alt + Z..M taps a chord.

chord-modes.recall: Synth page, the upper button beside the chord pads.
tips: For a new pad sound: stop the pads, change the sound, then tap a chord.
chord-modes.ask: How do the chord pads' modes work?

scope-readouts.title: SCOPE READOUTS
scope-readouts.summary: The numbers around the scope describe the real output.
scope-readouts.does: Top: volts and time per division (they follow the signal), trigger state and sample rate. Bottom: frequency, peak-to-peak level and note. They never change the sound.

use.text: Read them; the scope itself is the touch pad.

scope-readouts.recall: Synth page. Faint X and Y labels name the pad's axes.
tips: Frequency reads an octave low on sounds with a SUB: that is the wave's true repeat rate.
scope-readouts.ask: What are the numbers on the scope?

level-strip.title: LEVEL STRIP
level-strip.summary: A row of segments showing output loudness.
level-strip.does: 86 small segments under the header light up with the loudness of what you hear (output level). When the limiter is holding the sound back, a Limit tag shows beside the sound name. It is only a display; tapping does nothing.

use.text: Watch it; lower Master volume if it pegs.

level-strip.recall: Synth page, thin strip under the header. Master volume: System page.
level-strip.ask: How do I tell if the sound is too loud?

string-brackets.title: STRING BRACKETS
string-brackets.summary: Brackets that show where the pitch really is.
string-brackets.does: While a string sounds, a line wobbles across it and a pair of brackets sits round the true pitch, with a short trail. During a slide the brackets travel between note boxes. Boxes with bright frames are the key's root note.

use.text: Slide a note and watch the brackets.

string-brackets.ask: What are the brackets on the strings?

adsr.title: ADSR ENVELOPE
adsr.summary: Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release: the shape of a note's volume.
adsr.does: Attack: how fast a note fades in. Decay: how fast it falls to Sustain, the level held while the key is down. Release: the fade after you let go.

use.text: Sound page: Attack and Release; All parameters for Decay and Sustain.

adsr.recall: Sound page: Attack, Release. All parameters: Decay, Sustain.
tips: The filter has its own envelope: F.ATK, F.DEC, F.SUS, F.REL.
adsr.ask: What do attack, decay, sustain and release do?

panic.title: PANIC
panic.does: Stops all notes, the chord pads, latched pulses and loop playback, and clears Glitch and sustain. A loop being recorded is dropped; a finished loop is kept.

use.text: Backspace from any page.
System page, Panic.

panic.recall: System page, Panic; Backspace anywhere. Ctrl+L restarts the loop; a chord tap starts the pads again.
panic.ask: Everything is stuck. What do I press?

tempo.title: TEMPO (BPM)
tempo.summary: One tempo for the loop and the pulse pads' SYNC.
tempo.does: Beats per minute, 40 to 240, shared by the backing, the loop and the pulse pads' SYNC, plus delay times and the metronome. It appears on the Synth header, and on the Tune and Backing pages.

use.text: Tune page: − / + or Tap.
Ctrl+T taps a tempo; Ctrl+M clicks.

tempo.recall: Tune page; Ctrl+T anywhere. The beat lamp in the Synth header flashes on each beat while something plays.
tempo.ask: How do I set the tempo?

copilot.title: THE COPILOT (ROOK)
copilot.summary: An AI helper that can play and edit the app with you.
copilot.does: A copilot connects through a local control socket (off with --no-control). It can play notes, change the sound, shape pulse pads, and look at the screen. Its messages show in Chat, or in a strip at the bottom of any page.

use.text: Ctrl+Y jumps to Chat and back; type and press Enter.
Chat tab, type, tap Send.

copilot.recall: Chat tab; Ctrl+Y. The Chat tab shows an unread count. The strip never takes keys or touch.
tips: copilot: listening at the top right means one is connected.
copilot.ask: What can the copilot do for me?

undo-map.title: WHAT UNDOES WHAT
undo-map.summary: Each part of the app has its own undo.
undo-map.does: Sounds: Ctrl+Z (24 steps): New, Mutate, slots, favourites; not slider moves or Store. Loop: Ctrl+U per layer. Chord pads: tap a held chord or drone again.

use.text: Ctrl+Z (sound), Ctrl+U (loop).
Undo buttons on the Sound and Synth pages.

undo-map.recall: Sound page Undo; Synth page Undo (loop). Final: Store, Delete.
tips: Ctrl+Z is sound undo on every page.

ticker.title: THE TICKER
ticker.summary: Copilot messages appear over the bottom of any page.
ticker.does: A new copilot message shows in a two-line strip near the bottom for about seven seconds while you are on another page, and the Chat tab counts unread messages. It covers the bottom row of controls but takes no taps or keys.

use.text: Keep playing; open Chat to read and answer.

ticker.recall: Chat tab holds the full conversation. Ctrl+Y jumps there.
ticker.ask: Why did a message appear over my buttons?

status-box.title: STATUS BOX
status-box.summary: Facts about the audio output and the engine.
status-box.does: Shows the audio backend, sample rate, block size, output device, engine load, late blocks, the data folder and the last recording. If it says No real audio device, nothing will be heard.

use.text: Read only. Useful when sound stops or crackles.

status-box.recall: System page, the framed box in the middle.
tips: Late blocks above 0 mean the sound broke up.

listen-result.title: LISTEN RESULT
listen-result.summary: The key and tempo Listen guessed, with how sure it is.
listen-result.does: After Listen hears music it shows the most likely key and scale, the tempo, and a confidence for each. Low confidence means a guess. Use key, use tempo or use both to apply.

use.text: Tap Use key, Use tempo or Use both; Other key tries the next guess.

tips: Detection is an estimate: check by ear.
listen-result.ask: How good is the key detection?

help-rows.title: KEY LIST ROWS
help-rows.summary: A key (left) and what it does (right), for your keymap.
help-rows.does: Each row names a key or key combination and says what it does. The list follows your keymap, so if you remapped keys it shows your keys. Three lists: playing, commands, pulse and recording.

use.text: Tap a row to ask Rook about it.
Tap Next to read the next list.

tips: Q20 digits and arrows are on its number and symbol layers.

tour.title: THE TOUR
tour.summary: A picture of each page where every control explains itself.
tour.does: The tour shows a still picture of a page. Tap a control, or move with the arrow keys, and a card says what it does, how to use it by touch and keys, and how to find it again. Nothing in it is live.

use.text: Tap a control in the picture. Tap empty space to clear. Tabs at the top change page.
Arrows move, Tab cycles, Enter asks Rook, comma and period change page, Esc leaves.

tour.recall: Help page, Tour button. Ctrl+O from any page. Or ask Rook to show you.
tips: Start here walks through every page in order.
tour.ask: Can you walk me through the tour?

pulse-kinds.title: PULSE KINDS
pulse-kinds.summary: The eight sounds a pulse pad can be.
pulse-kinds.does: Click and knock: short struck sounds. Metal, snap and clap: noise and squares, like hats, snares and claps. FM ping: a glassy strike. Zap and sub thump: sines that fall in pitch.

use.text: TYPE on the Pulse page steps the selected pad through them.

pulse-kinds.recall: Pulse page. Pad n starts as the n-th kind; TONE means something different for each.
tips: Silence between hits is part of the sound: try slow rates.
pulse-kinds.ask: What are the eight kinds of pulse?

latch-sync.title: LATCH AND SYNC
latch-sync.summary: Pads that keep going, in time or free.
latch-sync.does: LATCH keeps the selected pad going: it is hit again RATE times a second. SYNC snaps every RATE to the tempo so latched pads fall on the beat; off, rates are exact Hz and drift against the loop.

use.text: Latch and Sync are soft keys on the Pulse page.

latch-sync.recall: Pulse page soft keys. Tap a latched pad to stop it; Backspace stops everything.
tips: Two latched pads at nearly the same free rate phase slowly against each other.
latch-sync.ask: How do LATCH and SYNC work together?

backing-modes.title: BACKING MODES
backing-modes.summary: What a chord tap does: Prog, Hold or Drone.
backing-modes.does: Prog queues up to eight chords that loop, each lasting its Beats per chord. Hold plays one chord until you pick another. Drone switches held bass notes on and off. A chord tap in Prog starts the backing at once.

use.text: Tap the mode button beside the chord pads.
Ctrl+B changes mode; Alt + Z..M plays a chord.

backing-modes.recall: Backing page, three buttons at the top. Clear all there empties the backing.
tips: The backing keeps the sound it started with; use Use current lead sound to match.
backing-modes.ask: How do I build a chord progression?
